question: Can established risk-control tests certify the same family-wise abstention claim as TRIAD's legacy Hoeffding-ratio controller with fewer independent calibration sequences, without losing validity when frames inside a sequence are dependent?
score_distribution: independent uniform(0,1) score per frame; true coverage C(t) = t

null.true_conditional_error: R(t) = 0.055 > alpha at every candidate, so every certification is false

dependent_frames.sequence_effect_definition: each sequence draws u ~ uniform(0,1); every frame error probability is multiplied by 2u, so the marginal q(s) and the truths R(t), C(t) are unchanged while errors cluster within sequences

seed_rule: cells ordered by error model (graded, null), regime (independent_frames, dependent_frames), then sequence count as listed; cell seed = master_seed + 1000 * cell_index; ChaCha8; draw order per sequence: u (dependent regime only), then per frame score then error uniform
selection_rule: qualifying candidate with the largest observed calibration coverage; ties keep the smaller threshold
false_certification: a certified selection t with R(t) > alpha or C(t) < minimum_coverage under the analytic truth
outcomes: false-certification rate with one-sided 99% Clopper-Pearson bounds
mean true coverage of the selected threshold, counting refusals as zero
dominance violations of hoeffding-bentkus over legacy-hoeffding-ratio

hypotheses.H1_validity: For legacy-hoeffding-ratio, hoeffding-bentkus and betting, in every cell the one-sided 99% Clopper-Pearson lower bound of the false-certification rate is at most delta. Any exceedance is a validity failure for that method.
hypotheses.H2_dominance: In every simulated dataset hoeffding-bentkus qualifies every candidate that legacy-hoeffding-ratio qualifies and reports a coverage lower bound at least as large. Any violation is an implementation failure.
hypotheses.H3_primary_efficiency: In the graded model with dependent frames, n80 for hoeffding-bentkus is at most half of n80 for legacy-hoeffding-ratio. n80 is the smallest listed sequence count whose certification rate is at least 0.80; if a method never reaches 0.80 its n80 is treated as exceeding 25000, and the hypothesis is then supported only if n80(hoeffding-bentkus) <= 12500.
hypotheses.H4_secondary_efficiency: The H3 criterion with betting in place of hoeffding-bentkus.
hypotheses.E1_exploratory: Expected but not a decision hypothesis: naive-frame-binomial, which treats dependent frames as independent, exceeds delta false certification in the null model with dependent frames.

planning_disclosure: The error model, targets and sequence grid were chosen from closed-form plug-in sample sizes (certify::plan) so that the grid brackets both methods. No Monte Carlo output existed when this protocol was frozen.
scope: A simulation of statistical procedures under their stated assumptions. It says nothing about sensors, hardware, drift, or whether any real scoring model is trustworthy.
